name: Diagnostic_VEC-UNT_1
questiontext:
The unit vector in the direction of \(\mathbf{a}={{CT:0}}\,\mathbf{i}+{{CT:1}}\,\mathbf{j}+{{CT:2}}\,\mathbf{k}\) is

\( \hat{\mathbf{a}}= \) [[input:ans1]] \(\mathbf{i}\) [[validation:ans1]] \(+\) [[input:ans2]] \(\mathbf{j}\) [[validation:ans2]] \(+\) [[input:ans3]] \(\mathbf{k}\). [[validation:ans3]]

Enter your answer exactly, using the sqrt function for square roots if necessary, for example inputting \( \sqrt{3} \) as sqrt(3).
generalfeedback: The magnitude of \(\mathbf{a}\), denoted \(\mid \mathbf{a} \mid\), is a positive quantity defined as \(\mid \mathbf{a} \mid = \sqrt{{{CT:0}}^2 + {{CT:1}}^2 + {{CT:2}}^2} = {{CT:3}}\). A unit vector in the direction of \(\mathbf{a}\) is \[\mathbf{\hat{a}}=\frac{\mathbf{a}}{\mid \mathbf{a} \mid} = {{CT:4}}\,\mathbf{i}+{{CT:5}}\,\mathbf{j}+ {{CT:6}}\,\mathbf{k}.\]

on_true.feedback: The vector you have input is parallel to the vector \(\textbf{a}\), and it is a unit vector, but it is in the opposite direction to \(\textbf{a}\).

The magnitude of this vector is

\[\sqrt{\left({@ans1@}\right)^2+\left({@ans2@}\right)^2+\left({@ans3@}\right)^2}={@ans_mag@}.\]

You may have divided by the square of a magnitude when you should have divided by a magnitude.

The magnitude of this vector is

\[\sqrt{\left({@ans1@}\right)^2+\left({@ans2@}\right)^2+\left({@ans3@}\right)^2}={@ans_mag@}.\]

It is a unit vector, but it is not in the correct direction.

on_false.feedback:
The magnitude of this vector is

\[\sqrt{\left({@ans1@}\right)^2+\left({@ans2@}\right)^2+\left({@ans3@}\right)^2}={@ans_mag@}\mbox{.}\]

But a unit vector has magnitude 1.
